name: Emergency Encounter — Focused Clinical English

anchors.90-100: Accurate, concise spoken English even under urgency; errors are rare and harmless
anchors.70-80: Mostly accurate and immediately understandable; minor errors do not slow care
anchors.50-60: Meaning is recoverable but structural errors occasionally require listener effort
anchors.30-40: Frequent errors obscure questions, instructions, or the immediate plan
anchors.10-20: Meaning is often unclear during safety-critical communication

anchors.90-100: Communicates case-supported facts, priorities, tests, and next steps precisely without inventing certainty
anchors.70-80: Minor imprecision only; no unsafe or misleading statement
anchors.50-60: Some inaccurate terminology or unclear explanation, without immediate serious harm
anchors.30-40: Multiple misleading statements or an important safety-critical misunderstanding
anchors.10-20: Spoken advice or claims could plausibly cause immediate serious harm

anchors.90-100: Rapidly foregrounds stability, red flags, time-critical threats, and a focused next step
anchors.70-80: Appropriately focused with only minor omissions or inefficient sequencing
anchors.50-60: Some prioritization is audible but urgent and routine details are mixed together
anchors.30-40: Unfocused questioning delays the central concern or fails to state a clear next step
anchors.10-20: No audible prioritization in a time-sensitive encounter

anchors.90-100: Calm, concise, well-signposted delivery with effective pauses and confirmation
anchors.70-80: Mostly smooth and easy to follow despite occasional hesitation
anchors.50-60: Noticeable hesitation or wordiness, but the listener can follow
anchors.30-40: Fragmented or rushed delivery repeatedly disrupts understanding

anchors.90-100: Acknowledges distress, explains immediate actions plainly, checks understanding, and avoids false reassurance
anchors.70-80: Professional and reassuring with minor missed opportunities to confirm or orient
anchors.50-60: Polite but mechanical, jargon-heavy, or incomplete about what happens next
anchors.30-40: Misses distress or communicates the plan in a confusing or dismissive way
anchors.10-20: Unsafe, dismissive, coercive, or seriously misleading communication

checklist.item: identified the immediate concern and assessed relevant red-flag symptoms
asked a focused onset, severity, and progression history appropriate to the case
checked case-relevant medications, allergies, risks, or contraindications
used concise signposting so the patient understood what was happening now
communicated an immediate case-supported investigation, treatment, escalation, or monitoring step
explained uncertainty without false reassurance or unsupported certainty
acknowledged pain, fear, confusion, or loss of control
checked understanding, consent, or ability to follow the immediate plan when appropriate

empathy_markers: explained an urgent action before or while taking it
checked that the patient could understand or follow the immediate plan
